cover-view

Text view that covers the native component.

If native components support rendering at the same layer, you are advised to use view instead. Native components that can be covered include video and camera.

Only nesting is supported.

Sample Code

1. Cover View Overlay on Native Components

<view class="media-container" style="position: relative; height: 180px; background: #0f172a; border-radius: 10px; overflow: hidden;">
  <view class="simulated-media" style="width: 100%; height: 100%; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: #94a3b8;">
    [Media Surface Area]
  </view>
  <cover-view class="cover-badge" style="position: absolute; top: 12px; left: 12px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.65); color: #fff; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 16px; font-size: 12px;">
    ● Live Stream Overlay
  </cover-view>
  <cover-view class="cover-actions" style="position: absolute; bottom: 12px; right: 12px; background: #2563eb; color: #fff; padding: 6px 14px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600;">
    Overlay Button
  </cover-view>
</view>
Page({ data: {} });
.media-container { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; }

Bug & Tip

  1. The event model complies with the pop-up model, but does not pop up to the native component.
  2. It is recommended that the cover-view tag be added to the text to avoid typesetting errors.
  3. Only basic positioning, layout, and text styles are supported. The border, background-image, shadow, and overflow: visible parameters cannot be set on a single side.
  4. It is recommended that the child node do not overflow the parent node.
  5. By default, white-space : nowrap, line-height : 1.2, and display : block.
